title: Ask for a little less certainty
brief: Build the smoothed target, the loss against it, and its gradient, then find where the loss is lowest.
hints: np.eye(num_classes)[targets] gives the one-hot rows. Scale them by 1 - eps, then add eps / num_classes to every entry.
The loss is the mean over rows of -(y_smooth * log_p).sum(axis=1). Use the provided log_softmax so large scores do not overflow.
The gradient is (p - y_smooth) / N with p = np.exp(log_softmax(logits)). Every row of the result sums to 0.
